correctness.rationale: For q>=2, ell>=2, n>=ell+1, deletion removes one ordered overlapping whole ell-mer, not a source symbol. A consistent received vector determines a unique length-n−1 z. Boundary reinsertion yields q left and q right parent words, with a single overlap iff z is constant. Inserting an interior ell-mer into consistent adjacency forces its length ell−1 prefix and suffix to coincide, hence it is a constant word; each strictly interior maximal constant run of length>=ell−1 contributes exactly one additional distinct parent and boundary-touching runs contribute none beyond the 2q boundary words. Therefore the consistent lists have sizes 2q−1 (constant) or 2q+J_{ell−1}(z). A single deleted read can produce inconsistency at only one adjacency, forcing the inserted read uniquely; attainable inconsistent y have one parent. Packing disjoint interior runs gives sharp max 2q+floor((n−3)/(ell−1)). Decomposing z into two boundary runs and a marked sequence of interior runs yields the stated rational F(t); counting distinct read-deletion outputs by maximal runs of identical original reads, and subtracting consistent parent incidences, proves the exact H formula for inconsistent receivers. Independent enumerations of source words/receivers for five parameter triples verified each positive parent-list size and all sample maxima. The argument specifies empty sums and n=ell+1 boundary.
